overall_note: Risk-weighted guess with a wide error bar. The page prefers the live figure in `docs/status.md` when it can read one.
machine: 14-inch MacBook Pro, M2 Pro (`T6020`, `apple,j414s`), Aurora Silicon Linux

goal.linux_night: 23% of the battery a night, about 1.7 days from full with the lid closed
goal.macos_night: 5.9 h lid closed on battery, 98.7% of it in S2R

phases.name: Remote hands
phases.short: Recovery without anyone at the Mac
phases.summary: The USB-PD board and smart plug were dropped (no extra hardware). Recovery comes from software instead, and it is proven.
done: Aura arms the hardware watchdog (WD1, 120 s) around `SYSTEM_SUSPEND`; a deliberate hang (image 27-hang) reset the Mac by itself
Every test image boots once; an early unit puts the default `boot.bin` back and checks its sha
Wi-Fi guard reboots a boot that never connects, with a 3-strike limit
The Raspberry Pi 5 streams the kernel log off the machine during risky runs
A dead-man switch (`deadman.sh`) reads the NVMe directly after each wake; if the disk is gone it pushes the kernel lines to the owner and resets the Mac. 3 of 3 OK in a real suspend
next: A sleep that never wakes in full S2R still needs the owner at the power key
After `slpa` a warm reset may not bring NVMe back; that needs a full power off
phases.gate: Unattended runs recover from a hang without hands.

phases.name: CPU_ON and CPU_OFF
phases.summary: CPU_OFF and CPU_ON work since image 47. Inside suspend all nine secondaries go off into Aura’s park and come back, every cycle of the Phase 2 gates. Runtime hotplug outside suspend has not been rerun.
done: Kernel: the PSCI-via-EFI RFC's six patches plus `t6020-j414s-psci.dts`
Aura: `psci.c`, `smp_psci_*`, `dt_set_psci()`; U-Boot: `efi_platform_register()`
CPU_ON of cpu1 to cpu9 in 0.25 s, also from a RAM-only boot that never touches the root filesystem
Found why RAM-only logs vanished: the ANS firmware caches writes until a clean `saveCtx` shutdown
The park uses deep WFI **with** retention; without it a core never came back properly (image 43)
The park restores `CYC_OVRD` before entering the kernel; re-onlined cores had inherited WFI_MODE 3 (image 47)
Kernel: a CPU_OFF that never returns no longer leaks the EFI virtmap preempt count (“scheduling while atomic” ×45 gone)
180 CPU_OFF/CPU_ON pairs per 20-cycle gate, 20 per core, 0 errors
next: Runtime hotplug (offline and online without suspend), 100 times per core, with `panic=0` and the watchdog
RVBAR re-entry for a core that really loses power
phases.gate: Each secondary offline and online 100 times, deep idle not worse, RVBAR re-entry works.

phases.name: SYSTEM_SUSPEND, SoC on
phases.short: Linux’s full suspend path with a firmware that hands back
phases.summary: Done on the full system. PSCI `SYSTEM_SUSPEND` through Aura’s EFI runtime handler, with the PMP on and all 10 CPUs: 20 of 20 cycles back in Linux, 0 device errors, through `echo mem` and through `systemctl suspend`. The SoC and DRAM stay up, so the drain is still near s2idle’s.
done: 20 of 20 suspend/resume cycles with Aura’s fixed wait (image 16), after a kernel fix for the EFI virtmap unwind
Wakes on the PMU RTC alarm (3 of 3, about 11 s for a 10 s alarm)
Wakes on the power key through the SMC mailbox line 865
Works with the PMP running, and through `systemctl suspend` with the sleep hooks
Deep WFI with state retention on the boot core (image 31)
Image 37 to 40 hung on cycle 1: an inline `dsb sy; isb; wfi` never woke. Back to `deep_wfi()` in image 41: 20 of 20
All 10 CPUs: 20 of 20 with image 47 and the CPU_OFF preempt fix, 0 device errors
The real path on all CPUs, `systemctl suspend -i` with the sleep hooks: 20 of 20
Image 48, the clean build with no diagnostic stamps: 20 of 20 on all CPUs. It is the reference image
phases.gate: 20 of 20 cycles back in Linux with no device errors.

phases.name: Trace macOS sleeping
phases.summary: The guest boots under the hypervisor with all 10 CPUs and the SMC and PMP tracers. Runs 7 to 11 captured macOS’s sleep entry in order. The wake is not visible under the hypervisor, so the raw-boot-mode risk is still open.
done: `macOSTest` volume (14.8.9; 14.8.3 is gone from Apple’s catalog) with Aura as its boot object
Three Aura and tracer fixes (`patches/hvsleep-trace`)
The ordered sleep entry: `slpw`, the PMP display power-down, `slpa`, `SetAPPower` 0x201, the CPU complexes off, deep WFI on every core
next: Find what restarts the AP on wake, and through which RVBAR
Answer whether iBoot arms the wake path for a raw image
phases.gate: An ordered list of every sleep and wake write, and a macOS wake under the hypervisor.

phases.name: Devices survive power loss
phases.summary: Each device has to come back after its power is really removed. The SMC handshake is mapped and NVMe already survives Phase 2’s suspends. The PMP wake is unsolved, and DCP is the long pole.
done: SMC: `WKTP` and `slpw` are harmless; `slpa` takes the storage away, so it goes last
PMP: RTKit IDLE acks in about 400 us
NVMe: `saveCtx` shutdown and resume, every Phase 2 cycle
next: PMP: macOS’s DART off/on and outbox steps around RUN, no reset
PCIe L2 entry and D3cold resume (no remove/rescan)
DCP: full shutdown and restart of its firmware
phases.gate: Each device passes 20 cycles with its power actually removed.

phases.name: Full S2R
phases.short: The SoC powers down, DRAM in self-refresh
phases.summary: Aura’s `SYSTEM_SUSPEND` gains the SoC steps in macOS’s order. Five `slpa` runs (11-04 and 11-05) came back on the alarm with the storage controller dead and the SoC AWAKE throughout. Image 52 then added macOS’s PMGR S2R timer and its all-core deep sleep: the timer is the first PMGR write the SoC acts on, resetting the Mac about 60 s later unless the S2R entry completes, and it does not complete even with every core powered down (runs D to F). The rest of macOS’s PMGR quiesce (clock gates, PLL-off, GPU) is next.
done: The PMGR, SMC and PMP sleep actions read from the macOS 13.5 kernelcache
Test kernel flag `macsmc_reboot.deep_steps`: `slpw` in prepare, `slpa` in suspend_late, `waka` on wake

First `slpa` inside a real suspend (image 48, all CPUs, 2026-11-04 21:32): the cycle came back, but the storage controller never powered up again (`IOP power acknowledgment failed: -62`, `ANS did not boot`). No watchdog fired; the owner reset the Mac by hand. Scrub clean
Image 49: suspends longer than two minutes, with a 60 s watchdog heartbeat (2 of 2 at 305 s)
Test kernel option `macsmc.pmp_sleep` (off): the PMP’s `SetAPPower`/`SetIOPPower` IDLE after `slpa`, staged for the next owner-attended run
Drain A/B on battery (2026-11-04/05): `deep` 1.365 W against `s2idle` 1.39 to 1.41 W. Parking the CPUs saves almost nothing; the rest is the SoC and its devices
SART save and restore across suspend (test kernel): a no-op on normal wakes (4 of 4 “kept”), ready to test after `slpa`

Second `slpa` run (image 49, 60 s alarm, 2026-11-05 07:01): it resumed on the alarm with the storage controller dead, like the first; the dead-man switch reset the Mac (first read as a reset without a resume, corrected at 15:57). Disk and FS clean
Image 50: the RVBAR path’s watchdog stages (10 s, 150 s) differ from every other reset, for the next `slpa` run; 2 of 2 on the normal path
macOS 13.5 watchdog kext read: PMU boot stage 0x50 at sleep, a 10 s SMC deadline at quiesce. Test kernel option `deep_steps` bit 8 (boot stage 0x50 across suspend) staged, off
First long suspend under Aura (image 50, 2026-11-05): 1 h 46 min on battery, 106 heartbeats, 1.444 W, 0 device errors; it woke early on an SMC mailbox event
Image 51: an RVBAR entry after a real S2R wake now resumes Linux (on the boot CPU) instead of resetting; ready for the owner-attended `slpa` runs
PMGR state counters readable from Linux (`pmgrcnt`): with the SoC up only `AWAKE` counts; `SLP_S2R` is the proof to look for in the next `slpa` run

Owner-attended runs A and B (image 51, 30 s alarm, 2026-11-05 15:14 and 15:21; B with the PMU boot stage 0x50): both resumed with the SoC up and the storage controller dead, and the dead-man switch reset the Mac. Boot stage 0x50 changed nothing. Disk clean

Run C (2026-11-05 16:00, `slpa` plus the PMP steps): the PMP firmware crashed on IDLE; resumed with the ANS dead; `apple-sart: entries kept`; PMGR counters `AWAKE` 65 s, `SLP_S2R` 0: the SoC never left AWAKE

Image 52 (2026-11-05 evening): Aura writes macOS’s PMGR S2R timer (MPMGR_AON + 0x4000) and/or sends every core into macOS’s deep sleep, set per suspend from Linux. Owner-attended runs D, D2, E, F: the timer resets the Mac about 60 s after it is written whatever the alarm does (D 86 s, D2 84.8 s with a 90 s alarm), also with every core powered down (E 85.7 s); the cores alone end in a WD1 reset (F 145.1 s). The first PMGR write the SoC acts on; the S2R entry still does not complete
next: Static: decode `AppleT6020PMGR::quiesceHW`’s clock-gate, PLL-off and GPU steps, and macOS’s AIC and PMU quiesce, into an image 53 step before the S2R timer; owner-attended run after
Static: what macOS does to start the ANS after a sleep wake, and what the PMP needs before IDLE (it crashed when sent IDLE after `slpa`)
After a first real S2R wake: restart the nine secondaries from Aura at runtime (design in the worklog, 2026-11-05 10:11)
More `slpa` runs only when the owner is ready to reset by hand
Lid wake, not tested separately yet
phases.gate: 20 of 20 cycles; lid, key, keyboard and alarm wakes; about 0.3 W on battery.

phases.name: Daily use
phases.summary: U-Boot passes Aura’s PSCI table on, Omarchy’s suspend uses `deep`, and the patches go to Aurora’s trees.

pieces.name: Timed wake
pieces.known: The PMU RTC alarm on SPMI irq 2, AIC 724. The “fired” bit must be cleared before re-arming. Upstream’s alarm is T6030-only, so the T602x patches are still needed.
pieces.next: Shape it for upstream; power-on from off is untested

pieces.name: Boot CPU hand-back
pieces.known: `SYSTEM_SUSPEND` returns through the kernel’s `cpu_resume`, 20 of 20 on all CPUs (image 48). It works with retention through `deep_wfi()`; an inline `dsb sy; isb; wfi` never woke (images 37 to 40). Powered down without retention, the core never re-enters at RVBAR (images 32 to 36).
pieces.next: A real S2R wake comes back through RVBAR; image 51 resumes the kernel from there, not reached yet

pieces.name: Wake sources
pieces.known: Deep WFI with AIC lines 724 (alarm) and 865 (SMC mailbox) unmasked. The power key wakes on 865.
pieces.next: Lid; stop the SMC’s early `Elec Cause` syslog wakes

pieces.name: AIC
pieces.known: Save and mask every bank, restore on resume (syscore). It runs on every Phase 2 cycle. Because it masks everything, wake detection has to come from the PMU/SMC side.

pieces.name: SMC handshake
pieces.known: `WKTP` and `slpw` are harmless. `slpa` makes the SMC cut the storage controller’s (ANS) power: in five runs inside a real suspend with all CPUs off (2026-11-04 and 05) the Mac resumed on the alarm and the ANS never booted again. On its own `slpa` does not start the SoC’s sleep (PMGR counters: `AWAKE` throughout). The dead-man switch’s reboot brings the disk back every time. `SetAPPower` IDLE to the SMC is acked and safe.
pieces.next: The PMGR’s own entry after `slpa`, and how macOS restarts the ANS after a wake

pieces.name: PMP
pieces.known: IDLE works in s2idle (acks in about 400 us). Sent after `slpa`, IDLE crashed the PMP firmware (run C, 2026-11-05). RUN alone woke it 0 of 3. Gating `ps_pms_sram` does not restart it, and a PMGR reset of `ps_pmp` crashes the SoC.
pieces.next: Static: what the PMP needs before IDLE, then its wake

pieces.name: Secondary CPUs
pieces.known: CPU_OFF parks the core in Aura’s retention deep WFI loop; CPU_ON hands it back through the spin table, with `CYC_OVRD` restored first. 20 of 20 suspend cycles with all nine.
pieces.next: Runtime hotplug outside suspend; RVBAR re-entry after real power loss

pieces.name: PMGR quiesce, S2R timer
pieces.known: The S2R timer (1 to MPMGR_AON + 0x4000) works from Aura: it resets the SoC about 60 s later unless the S2R entry completes (runs D, D2, E). With `slpa` and every core powered down macOS’s way the entry still does not complete. The clock gates, PLL-off and GPU steps of `quiesceHW` are not done yet.
pieces.next: Decode and add `quiesceHW`’s remaining steps, then an owner-attended run

pieces.name: Devices
pieces.known: s2idle only. DCP cannot resume from power loss today.

findings.title: The gap is SoC sleep itself
findings.body: Awake idle matches macOS once the PMP runs (5.38 W against 5.57 W, SoC 1.22 W on both). The lid-closed gap is not the devices.

findings.title: s2idle’s 1.4 W is power left on, not wakes
findings.body: The 3.2 wakes a second come from the AOP’s ambient-light and lid-angle reports and cost milliwatts. The PMP doesn’t change the drain.

findings.title: macOS tells the PMP when the system sleeps
findings.body: Read from the macOS 13.5 kernelcache: the full order of sleep and quiesce actions, the SMC `MBSE` handshake, PMGR’s last write, and the PMP’s RTKit IDLE (0x201), which is Linux’s unused `apple_rtkit_idle()`.

findings.title: `slpa` takes the storage away
findings.body: After `slpa` every NVMe access fails: in s2idle (10-22) and in five real suspends (11-04 and 05), where the Mac resumed on the alarm and the storage controller never booted again. A reboot from Linux (the dead-man switch’s) brings it back. On its own `slpa` does not put the SoC to sleep, so it cannot be the last step by itself.

findings.title: The PMP’s wake from IDLE is a power cycle
findings.body: RUN alone woke it 0 of 3. Gating its SRAM did not restart it, and resetting `ps_pmp` crashed the SoC. `ps_pmp` is pinned on by iBoot.

findings.title: ISR_EL1 is blind at EL2 under VHE
findings.body: With IMO/FMO set, Aura saw only the virtual pending state. The fix was to watch the AIC’s HW_STATE for the alarm line.

findings.title: The kernel masks the whole AIC for suspend
findings.body: `aic_syscore_suspend` masks every line, as macOS does. In real S2R the wake must be detected from the PMU/SMC side.

findings.title: A core powered down without retention doesn’t come back on an IRQ
findings.body: Across images 32 to 36 the boot core never re-entered at RVBAR. Secondaries only return through a PMGR CPU-start written by another core.

findings.title: NVMe drops cached writes on a hard reset
findings.body: The ANS firmware caches until a clean `saveCtx` shutdown. That explained the lost logs and the filesystem damage after hotplug hangs.

findings.title: The PMU RTC alarm is the timed wake
findings.body: Linux had no driver for the alarm macOS uses for dark wakes. `rtcwake -m freeze -s 30` woke after about 31 s, 3 of 3.

findings.title: Parked cores need retention, and must not keep WFI_MODE 3
findings.body: The October hotplug deaths came from two things: the CPU_OFF park powered cores down without retention, and a re-onlined core inherited `CYC_OVRD` WFI_MODE 3 from the park. With both fixed, all nine secondaries go off and come back every suspend cycle.

findings.title: A CPU_OFF that never returns leaks a preempt count
findings.body: The kernel’s EFI call path disables preemption around the firmware call. A successful CPU_OFF never comes back, so the re-onlined core started with one count too many (“scheduling while atomic”, once per core per cycle). Fixed in the test kernel.

findings.title: `slpa` alone does not put the SoC to sleep
findings.body: With every CPU in Aura and the boot core in deep WFI, `slpa` still left the SoC running. On the wake `waka` is acked, but the storage controller never acks its power-on (`IOP power acknowledgment failed: -62`). macOS does more between `slpa` and the power-down: `SetAPPower` and `SetIOPPower` to the PMP, the CPU stops and the PCPM clears.

findings.title: A live kernel with no disk is not a hang
findings.body: After the `slpa` run the watchdogs saw a healthy kernel, so nothing reset the Mac for about 15 min. Unattended `slpa` runs need a dead-man switch tied to the disk.

findings.title: The watchdog cannot cover a long sleep by itself
findings.body: WD1 counts 32 bits at 24 MHz, about 178 s at most. Aura now wakes on the EL2 physical timer every 60 s, re-arms the dog and sleeps again, so suspends of any length keep the safety net.

findings.title: Parking the CPUs alone saves almost nothing
findings.body: Suspend to RAM with every CPU in Aura’s deep WFI drew 1.365 W over 30 min on battery, and `s2idle` 1.390 and 1.413 W in the same boot. The gap to macOS’s 0.24 W is the SoC and DRAM staying up, which only the SoC steps (`slpa` and after) can close.

findings.title: A PMGR gate alone does not lose the storage controller
findings.body: genpd switched `ps_ans2` (the ANS, its mailbox and its SART) off in each of last night’s 4 suspends, and NVMe came back every time. So `slpa` takes away more than that gate does, perhaps the rail itself. The SART’s entries (8 of 16 used) are the first thing to check after the next `slpa` run.

findings.title: macOS writes the storage controller’s SART back on every start
findings.body: `IOSARTMapper::_setActive(true)` (13.5) copies the SART’s 16 config and 16 address words the first time, and writes them back every later time. The ANS start after sleep runs it. So macOS expects the SART to lose its entries in S2R, and the Linux SART driver had nothing for that. The test kernel now does the same.

findings: macOS tells the PMU the AP is asleep (`IOPMUBootStage` 0x50) in its sleep action, and gives the SMC a 10 s AP-watchdog deadline at the last quiesce step; Linux leaves 0x30 (“OS running”) through suspend, so a reset from sleep counts as a boot error

The PMGR’s AP wake-source mask (`0x29e00400c`, 1 = disabled) is 0 under Linux. macOS’s value, with only its 22 sources enabled, also stops the alarm and the EL2 timer from waking the boot CPU out of Aura’s deep WFI

The PMGR keeps per-state time counters (`AWAKE`, `SLP_S2R`, `SYS_S2R_AOP`, …), off under Linux. Turned on, they show the SoC stays AWAKE through Aura’s suspend and s2idle; in an `slpa` run that comes back they can prove a real S2R
PMGR counters after `slpa` plus the PMP steps (run C, 2026-11-05): `AWAKE` the whole 65 s, `SLP_S2R` 0. `slpa` does not put the SoC to sleep by itself; it only takes the storage controller down
The SART is intact after `slpa` (run C: `entries kept across suspend`); the ANS failure after `slpa` has another cause

The PMGR’s S2R timer (1 to MPMGR_AON + 0x4000, macOS’s `startS2RTimer`) resets the SoC about 60 s after it is written unless the S2R entry completes, whatever the alarm does (runs D, D2; 2026-11-05). With every core powered down macOS’s way it still resets (run E); the cores alone end in a WD1 reset (run F)
rules: Never remove and rescan PCI devices: it kills Wi-Fi until a reboot.
No `slpa` runs unless the owner is ready to reset the Mac by hand.
Keep a `.keep` file in module trees pacman doesn’t own.
No hotplug tests on a boot that can hurt the root filesystem.
Check the ESP sha after every copy, and refuse to suspend on the default image.
Test GRUB entries use `panic=0`, so a panic hangs and the watchdog stamps tell where it died.
unknowns: Whether iBoot arms the wake path (reconfig engine, boot CPU RVBAR) for a raw image as it does for a kernelcache.
What starts the SoC’s sleep: not `slpa` alone (the PMGR counters stay in `AWAKE`); presumably the PMGR’s S2R entry, which Aura does not do yet. And what restarts the AP on wake, through which RVBAR.
What the reconfig engine runs on `SLP_S2R`, and what each quiesce action writes.
Whether a DCP with nothing attached can be shut down and restarted.
What the PMP’s VLPM tunables control.
Why an inline `dsb sy; isb; wfi` in `SYSTEM_SUSPEND` never woke when `deep_wfi()` does.
What brings NVMe back after `slpa`: not the SART (kept, run C); the ANS CPU never reaches status 0x28
What the PMP needs before IDLE: sent after `slpa`, IDLE crashed it (run C)
